eventMetadata.context_description:
**The near-certain market consensus on 31°C as Hong Kong’s highest temperature on September 4, 2026, stems from post-event confirmation by the Hong Kong Observatory (HKO), the authoritative source for official daily maximum temperatures.** 

HKO measurements at its headquarters station, taken under standardized conditions with calibrated instruments, recorded a peak of 31°C amid typical early-September conditions featuring moderate humidity, variable winds, and limited cloud cover that allowed sufficient solar heating without strong convective cooling. This aligns closely with climatological norms for the period (around 30–31°C) and contrasts with neighboring days showing slightly lower or higher peaks driven by passing showers or clearer skies. 

Traders’ skin-in-the-game assessment treats the HKO figure as definitive for market resolution, which uses the observatory’s official daily maximum. The only realistic challenges would involve an extremely rare post-publication data revision by HKO due to instrument calibration issues or a shift to an alternate station reading, neither of which has precedent in recent records.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent heavy rain, thunderstorms, and extensive cloud cover across Taipei on September 6 are suppressing daytime heating, with official forecasts and real-time observations converging on a maximum of 25–26°C. Widespread precipitation enhances evaporative cooling while thick cloud layers limit solar radiation reaching the surface, preventing temperatures from approaching the seasonal average near 30°C. Current surface observations hover near 25°C amid 90–100% humidity and moderate northwest winds, aligning with the market’s strong 69.5% implied probability for 25°C and 23.3% for 26°C. Any break in rainfall timing or localized clearing could nudge the peak slightly higher, but model consensus favors continued suppression through the afternoon.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Cape Town International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 6 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=fact

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Clear, sunny conditions under a strong high-pressure system are driving Cape Town's September 6 maximum temperature toward the mid-20s Celsius, with official and model guidance from sources such as GFS indicating afternoon peaks of 23–26 °C under light southeasterly flow and very low humidity. Recent hourly observations and short-range forecasts show steady warming through midday, with some ensemble members and local stations reaching 27–29 °C briefly, creating the narrow distribution around 26–28 °C. Spring climatology for the region features occasional berg-wind episodes that can add several degrees, yet the current stable pattern and absence of significant moisture limit upside risk. Traders have priced the 27 °C outcome highest at 48.5 % implied probability because it aligns with the most probable model consensus for the daily high, while the 26 °C bucket captures downside revisions if readings are taken at the cooler airport site. Updated afternoon observations and any final model runs will determine whether the market shifts toward the 28 °C tail.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models from agencies including Météo-France and global ensembles such as GFS indicate a maximum temperature in Paris on September 7 clustered around 28–29 °C, driven by partly cloudy skies, moderate westerly flow, and residual warmth from the preceding day’s 28–30 °C readings. This places the market-implied probability of 28 °C (52.5 %) ahead of 29 °C (27.0 %), reflecting tight model agreement and limited spread in ensemble outputs. Above-average conditions relative to the September climatological high of 22.7 °C further support these outcomes, while the modest 14 % chance for 27 °C accounts for possible slight cooling from increased cloud cover or light showers. Updated model runs and official observations released on September 6 reinforce trader positioning ahead of final resolution.

**Forecast models and official outlooks position 33°C as the most likely daily maximum for Singapore on September 7 under prevailing Southwest Monsoon conditions.** 

Persistent dry weather, southeasterly winds, and above-normal seasonal temperatures across Southeast Asia support afternoon heating to the low-to-mid 30s Celsius, consistent with Singapore's Meteorological Service guidance of 33–35°C maxima on most early-September days. Recent model runs (including GFS and ECMWF ensembles) and climatological baselines show typical peaks near 32–34°C when cloud cover remains limited and showers stay localized or absent. Haze from regional fires adds minor radiative forcing but has not altered core temperature guidance. With resolution tied to official observations, trader consensus reflects the narrow range of credible outcomes around the seasonal mean, tempered by uncertainty in exact cloud and shower timing.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Qingdao Jiaodong International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 7 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=zsqd

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent numerical weather prediction runs from the China Meteorological Administration and global ensembles show stable high-pressure dominance over the Yellow Sea region, with clear skies and light northeasterly winds favoring daytime maxima near 28°C for Qingdao on September 7. Model consensus points to modest diurnal warming under mostly sunny conditions, though small spread in boundary-layer mixing and local sea-breeze effects creates uncertainty around the precise peak. Trader sentiment reflected in the 31°C and 30°C outcomes captures this variability plus potential warm bias at urban or observatory stations relative to airport readings, while lower probabilities for 32°C+ align with limited intensification potential absent stronger southerly flow. Updated short-range guidance and final station observations tomorrow will refine resolution.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the San Francisco International Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 7 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=ksfo

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service and NOAA model guidance points to a San Francisco high near 78–80°F on September 7, supporting the market’s tight clustering around the 78–81°F outcomes. Persistent onshore flow and a deepening marine layer are expected to limit inland warming, while subtle differences in low-level wind speed and timing of any high-pressure ridge strengthening could shift the peak by 1–2°F. Ensemble consensus from the GFS and ECMWF shows limited spread, though coastal stratus clearance rates remain a key uncertainty. September climatology for the city averages near 74–76°F, placing the implied range modestly above normal. Fresh model runs and afternoon observations will refine the final reading before market resolution.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Chaudhary Charan Singh Intl Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 8 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=vilk

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Active monsoon conditions across northern India, with widespread cloud cover, frequent thunderstorms, and heavy rainfall, are suppressing daytime heating in Lucknow and positioning 31°C as the leading market outcome at 41% implied probability. Official forecasts from the India Meteorological Department and models indicate a high of around 30–32°C on September 8 amid 70–80% rain chances, consistent with recent observations of maxima near 30–31°C under similar unsettled weather. This aligns with typical September climatology of 33°C averages moderated by peak monsoon moisture, while drier breaks could allow brief spikes toward 33–34°C. Updated model runs and next IMD briefings will refine these probabilities ahead of resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent monsoon-driven cloud cover and scattered thunderstorms are the main factors keeping Manila's September 8 maximum temperature tightly clustered around 28–30 °C in trader pricing. eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service and ensemble forecasts for Miami on September 8 point to a high near 88–90°F amid typical late-summer convective patterns, with afternoon thunderstorms likely after morning clearing. Abundant tropical moisture (precipitable water above 2 inches) and a weak steering flow favor scattered to numerous storms that can limit peak heating through cloud cover and evaporative cooling, creating the tight clustering between the 88–89°F and 90–91°F bins. Recent days have seen highs in the low 90s under similar setups, but any earlier or stronger sea-breeze convergence or lingering cloud debris from overnight activity could suppress readings into the upper 80s, while delayed convection or stronger insolation would support the low 90s. Model guidance shows modest spread in storm timing, sustaining the near-even implied probabilities for these adjacent ranges.

title: Highest temperature in Denver on September 8?
description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Buckley Space Force Base Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 8 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=kbkf

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This setup creates tight uncertainty across the 82–91°F bins, as small variations in cloud cover, timing of any storms, or downslope warming could shift the peak by a few degrees.
